title: Painter's Partition (Binary Search)
statement:
You are given `n` boards in a row. Board `i` has length `boards[i]`, and painting a board takes one unit of time per unit of length. You have `k` painters who all paint at the same speed and work **at the same time**.

The boards are assigned to painters under these rules:

- Every board is painted by exactly one painter.
- Each painter paints a **contiguous** block of boards (possibly an empty block, so a painter may stay idle). Painters cannot split a board and the order of the boards cannot change.
- The total time of the job is the time at which the last painter finishes, i.e. the **largest total length** assigned to a single painter.

Return the **minimum possible total time** over all valid assignments.

**Follow-up:** the same idea applies to splitting any workload among `k` workers (for example, packing pages into `k` shelves or shipping packages within a number of days). Think about why the answer can be found by binary searching on the time rather than on the array.
input_format:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `boards[0], ..., boards[n-1]`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum possible total time.

examples.explanation: Split into [7, 2, 5], [10] and [8, 4]. The totals are 14, 10 and 12, so the job takes 14. No split does better: a limit of 13 would force [7, 2] then [5, 10] = 15 > 13.
[10, 20, 30] and [40] gives 60 and 40; [10, 20] and [30, 40] gives 30 and 70. The best maximum is 60.
Each painter takes one board, so the answer is the longest board.

hints: If you fix a time limit T, you can check greedily whether k painters are enough: give each painter as many consecutive boards as fit within T.
Feasibility is monotone in T: if T works, every larger T works. The answer lies between the longest board and the sum of all boards.
Binary search on T using the greedy check; the smallest feasible T is the answer.
brute:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n, k = int(data[0]), int(data[1])
a = [int(x) for x in data[2:2 + n]]
pre = [0]
for x in a:
    pre.append(pre[-1] + x)
INF = float('inf')
dp = [[INF] * (n + 1) for _ in range(k + 1)]
dp[0][0] = 0
for j in range(1, k + 1):
    for i in range(n + 1):
        best = INF
        for p in range(i + 1):
            if dp[j - 1][p] < INF:
                best = min(best, max(dp[j - 1][p], pre[i] - pre[p]))
        dp[j][i] = best
print(dp[k][n])
